name: jev_mem_traversal
description: Jev-Mem System-One read-side traversal. Port of memory/jev_questions.traversal_questions (4 noul per candidate) over up to 2 frontier candidates per call — Jev-Mem batches these inside a Python loop; the DSL port expands 2 candidates inline (8 noul) so callers that walk a 2-deep frontier can run the same scoring without writing Rust. If you need more than 2 candidates, run this spec once per candidate pair, or hand-roll a `heuristic.extract_numeric` version per edge weight. `copy_keys` emits all 8 calibrated probabilities into state; the caller applies Jev-Mem's weighted `transition_weights` scoring externally. The primary_q is the first candidate's relevance signal.

cand_0_relevance.instructions: Does `candidates[0].content` contain a fact needed to answer `query`?
cand_0_relevance.truthy: Direct answer evidence or a necessary intermediate fact.
cand_0_relevance.falsy: Only topic overlap or unrelated content.

cand_0_relation_usefulness.instructions: Does the stated graph relation of `candidates[0]` connect `evidence` to information useful for `query`?
cand_0_relation_usefulness.truthy: The relation and its direction support an answer-relevant connection.
cand_0_relation_usefulness.falsy: A graph edge exists but has no demonstrated usefulness for this question.

cand_0_new_information.instructions: Does `candidates[0].content` add an answer-relevant detail absent from `evidence`?
cand_0_new_information.truthy: A distinct relevant detail or missing reasoning link.
cand_0_new_information.falsy: Only duplicated evidence or irrelevant new details.

cand_0_supports_current_evidence.instructions: Does `candidates[0].content` independently corroborate a claim in `evidence` relevant to `query`?
cand_0_supports_current_evidence.truthy: Provides compatible corroborating evidence for a specific claim.
cand_0_supports_current_evidence.falsy: No specific corroboration, or contradicts that claim.
